distinction_statement: Innovation changes the option space while improvement refines an existing path
decision_consequence: Weak distinction overcounts routine improvements as innovation

distinction_statement: Impact refers to consequential change while outputs are activities or deliverables
decision_consequence: Activity may be mistaken for outcome

distinction_statement: Resilience may include adaptation whereas stability preserves current state
decision_consequence: Strategy may preserve brittle or harmful arrangements

distinction_statement: Alignment means coherent fit with strategy whereas agreement may be social consensus
decision_consequence: False consensus may be treated as strategic coherence

distinction_statement: Transformation changes structure while modernization may only update tools or language
decision_consequence: Incremental upgrades may be overstated as structural change

distinction_statement: Sustainability includes limits and responsibility not merely continuation
Trust involves credibility and reliability beyond momentary satisfaction
decision_consequence: Satisfaction scores may hide institutional distrust

distinction_statement: Efficiency concerns resource use while effectiveness concerns achieving the right outcome
decision_consequence: Cost reduction may undermine strategic purpose

distinction_statement: Value is broader than price and may include trust knowledge legitimacy or systems benefit
decision_consequence: Pricing logic may miss actual value drivers

distinction_statement: Participation requires influence while consultation may only collect input
decision_consequence: Symbolic inclusion may be mistaken for shared design
